subject: est.rf with one marker against all

messages.author: 014d6d91b6813334
messages.subject: est.rf with one marker against all
parts:
Hi Karl,

Fig. 8 in your great introduction to genetic map construction provides an extremely useful way of determining contig order to generate larger scaffolds. I simply plot recombination frequency of a marker on each end of a contig against all markers. I have been using this approach with great success. 

But, some of my datasets are too large (>25,000 markers) to perform est.rf. I am wondering if there is an established R/qtl routine for calculating recombination fraction of one marker against all markers without perform est.rf on the entire dataset. This would be extremely useful.

Thanks, David

messages.author: 04e62c3b36bb17bf
messages.subject: Re: est.rf with one marker against all
parts:
Hi David, 
Your approach sounds really interesting. 

You've run into a standard problem - 25k x 25k matrices are too large to estimate in R. I find, 10k x 10k is about as big as I can go. 
Why not try to cull your matrix? You definitely won't need 25k markers in your final map ... more likely 5k at most. 

You could apply qtlTools::dropSimilarMarkers (http://lovelleeb.weebly.com/qtltools) to each chromosome (assuming each chr is <10k markers). 
You could then push the resultant smaller genotype matrix through your pipeline.
John

messages.subject: Re: est.rf with one marker against all
parts:
Thanks for the suggestion. I have ~100 contigs, ~1000 individuals, and have already thinned the markers pretty aggressively. Though, more thinning might help.
I think I have another approach that might work. I will simply compare contigs pairwise and group those with rf << 0.5 as part of same linkage group. I expect 4 linkage groups. I should then be able to est.rf on all contigs from single linkage group. Just a little bit of R coding for all pairwise comparisons that perhaps even I can handle.

messages.author: 25e13e522040f0b9
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: est.rf with one marker against all
parts:
Hi David,

If you have a tentative map, you can do rounds of MSG followed by est.rf using only markers at ends of each contig and then the interactive plot.rf to find better positions for contigs. Repeat this until you can't find better positions for contigs.
I have the code I used for anchoring scaffolds into chromosomes in Peromyscus if you want it.

Andrés
